newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine gas project seen delayed by bid process.
newsitem.headline: Philippine gas project seen delayed by bid process.

text.p: The conversion of a mothballed Philippine nuclear power plant into a huge gas-fired facility will likely face delays if a bidding process is adopted, Energy Secretary Francisco Viray warned on Sunday.

Viray told reporters the state Committee on Privatisation opposed a proposal by state-run National Power Corp (Napocor) to forego a bidding and enter into a negotiated contract to convert the 620-megawatt Philippine Nuclear Power Plant into a 1,500-mw gas-fired plant.
The energy department and Napocor wanted a negotiated contract with Shell Philippines Exploration B.V. (Spex) and Occidental Philippines Inc for the conversion.
Spex and Occidental are the operators of the country's biggest commercial gas find, from which fuel for the converted power plant will be sourced.
Spex is the oil exploration arm of Royal Dutch Shell group while Occidental Philippines is a unit of Occidental Petroleum Corp.

The nuclear power plant located in Bataan province near the capital Manila and built in the 1980s was never commissioned by Napocor due to a legal battle with its builders, Westinghouse Electric Corp and Burns & Roe.
